Variants.Content: Rosby City is located in the hinterland of the royal territory east of King's Landing. It is a castle territory with the lord's manor, farmland and roads leading to the capital as its skeleton. It does not handle thousands of people like the Red Castle, but it can affect the daily supply of King's Landing with grain, livestock, pack teams and local knights. The nobles of the crown often have their names obscured by the shadow of the capital: they are close to the throne and therefore more susceptible to taxation, conscription, marriage alliances and palace battles. Rosby embodies this situation - a seemingly peaceful field, but behind it is connected to Blackwater Bay, King's Road and urban markets. This should not be used to predict the choice of any family or character.

Entry Rosby Castle Local families also relied on the King's Market, Blackwater Bay shipping, orchards, field rents, and the road to King's Landing; if any road, well, or wharf failed, the cost would fall first on them.

Entry Rosby Castle If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

The traces left by generations of people in Rosby City are half hidden in the stone walls, wooden beams, iron doors, tombs and seams left by generations of repairs, and half hidden in the Seven Gods, royal decrees and the flags that have been constantly changed since the conquest. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Rosby Castle They care about the King's Capital Market, Blackwater Bay shipping, orchards, field rents and the road leading to King's Landing. They also look at whether seeds are left after the grain collection and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see the coat of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
